literal: Like a tree that becomes an unfailing medicine in all its parts, indeed, is wealth, if it reaches the hands of a person of great nobility.
translation: If wealth reaches the hands of a person of great nobility, it is like a tree whose every part becomes an unfailing medicine.
modern: பெருந்தன்மையானவரிடத்தில் செல்வம் சேர்ந்தால், அது தனது எல்லா உறுப்புகளும் மருந்தாகிப் பயன்படும் மரத்தைப் போன்றதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet compares the wealth of a benevolent person to a medicinal tree. A medicinal tree is one whose bark, leaves, root, and fruit all serve as remedies without failing. Similarly, when wealth reaches a person of great nobility, every bit of it is used to alleviate the suffering of others. The word 'tappā' highlights that the tree never fails to heal, just as the noble person's wealth never fails to help those in need.
